item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is closer to the frozen contract because it preserves FilesService.Add unchanged, explicitly validates Upload inputs, and limits the behavioral change to the new convenience API. B intentionally changes Add by eagerly buffering every caller-supplied body, which directly violates the requirement to preserve Add’s existing behavior and expands scope.","reasons":["A adds the exact Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and preserves FilesOption handling and response semantics.","A explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before constructing or sending a request.","B changes Add to io.ReadAll every body before request dispatch, altering streaming, memory usage, context-cancellation timing, and reader-error timing despite the explicit preservation requirement.","B’s changelog, README, and Add retry test confirm that the forbidden Add behavior change is intentional rather than incidental scope churn blocks merge readiness before review polish is considered; none of B’s stronger documentation/tests compensate for this contract violation. B also routes Upload through a new private add method rather than the required existing Add method."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add’s option, request, decoding, and missing-data logic instead of routing through Add, creating maintenance drift and violating an explicit contract item.","The retry test verifies only the number of requests; it does not read and compare multipart content on every attempt, so it would not catch an empty replayed body.","The retry test omits RetryAllMethods: true and there are no visible validation or source-reader-error tests."],"risks_b":["Eager buffering in Add is an unnecessary API behavior change and can impose substantial memory use for custom multipart bodies.","Upload bypasses the public Add method, contrary to the required routing pattern.","Validation is delegated to multipartbody.NewFile rather than being visibly enforced by Upload, and there are no explicit validation or source-reader-error tests."]}
